primitives.note: Ferocity: every basic ability cast (or a Savagery empowered attack) generates a stack, capped at 4; the 4th stack consumed by the next basic ability empowers it.
Consuming max Ferocity grants the empowered ability 'an additional cast' on top of its normal effect.

P: Unseen Predator arms the next basic attack with a leap and extended range; Q: Savagery arms the next basic attack with bonus physical damage that can crit; R: Thrill of the Hunt arms the next basic attack with 100% AD bonus damage and armor shred.
Savagery resets Rengar's basic attack timer.
Savagery grants 40% bonus AS for the next two attacks; the Ferocity-empowered cast grants an additional ~50-101%-by-level bonus AS for 5s.
Base and Ferocity-empowered damage instances of the stab (Q), roar (W), bola (E), and bonus attack (R) are each fixed on-cast/on-hit damage values.
Thrill of the Hunt's bonus attack shreds target armor for 4s, increasing subsequent physical damage taken.

Bonetooth Necklace grants bonus AD = trophies^2 (up to 5, or 6 with Head of Kha'Zix); trophies are earned from unique champion takedowns, impossible to earn organically in a 1-target dummy/survival fight, so a starting stack count must be assumed.

Unseen Predator is granted while in brush or (after a 2s delay) while Thrill of the Hunt's camouflage is active; whether the simulated fight starts with brush/opener access decides whether the leap-attack empowerment is available at all.
Savagery's first empowered basic attack 'will critically strike, dealing increased damage based on his critical strike chance'.

needsBespoke.why: Ferocity is a single shared resource generated by casting ANY of P/Q/W/E/R (or a Savagery attack) that empowers whichever basic ability is cast next, with a non-refreshing 1s-per-stack timer protected by a 10s in-combat grace period, and it grants an extra cast of whatever ability consumes it. No single closed-list primitive captures a resource shared across four different abilities with different empowered payloads, a bugged non-refresh stacking rule, and a conditional recast; modeling it requires bespoke state tracking layered on top of the listed primitives (nth-hit-or-cast + recast-or-multipart + empowered-attack combined).

unsettled.question: Does the simulated damage fight grant Rengar brush access (continuous Unseen Predator) at all, or is Unseen Predator only available via R's 2s-delayed camouflage on its long cooldown?
options: No brush in the arena; Unseen Predator is only active during/after R's camouflage window
Assume Rengar starts in or has constant access to brush, so Unseen Predator (leap empowered attack) is available for the whole 15s
quotes: After a 2-second delay, he also becomes {{tip|camouflage|camouflaged}} and gains ''{{ai|Unseen Predator|Rengar}}''.

unsettled.question: What Bonetooth Necklace trophy count should be assumed at the start of the fight, since the 1v1 dummy/survival fight offers no takedowns to earn trophies naturally?
options: Assume 0 trophies (no bonus AD from Bonetooth)
Assume a simulator-configured fixed trophy count (e.g. a typical late-game value) to reflect realistic play
quotes: ''Trophies'' grant {{sti|{{as|'''bonus''' attack damage}}}} equal to {{as|... formula=(Number of Trophies) * (Number of Trophies) ... '''bonus''' AD}}.

unsettled.question: Should the simulator model the currently-documented bug where Ferocity stacks from back-to-back casts do not refresh the 1s expiry timer, or the apparently intended always-refreshing behavior?
options: Model live/current behavior: only the first cast in a rapid sequence refreshes the 1s timer, so out-of-combat back-to-back casting can still let a stack expire
Model intended behavior: every qualifying cast refreshes the 1s timer, guaranteeing Ferocity accumulates to 4 as long as casts are close together
quotes: stacking up 4 times but not refreshing on subsequent triggers {{bug|2}}
* While out of combat, if abilities are used one after the other, only the first will count towards the 1 second {{as|Ferocity|buzzword3}} timer, without refreshing from the second cast.

proposal: Open the fight by casting R (Thrill of the Hunt) immediately if it is available, to mark the dummy for a free 100% AD bonus-damage attack plus a 4s armor shred, accepting its 2s delay before camouflage/Unseen Predator activates.
Land a basic attack (or Savagery-empowered attack) to consume R's bonus-damage mark and apply the armor shred as early as possible.

Cast Q (Savagery) on cooldown throughout the fight: it deals bonus on-hit physical damage, grants two stacks of bonus attack speed, resets the basic attack timer, and generates a Ferocity stack each cast.
Weave in E (Bola Strike) and W (Battle Roar) on their own cooldowns between Savagery casts and basic attacks, since both deal direct damage and each also generates a Ferocity stack.

Whenever Ferocity reaches 4 stacks, cast whichever of Q/W/E/R is next up (or is about to come off cooldown) to consume it into its Ferocity-empowered, higher-damage version and gain its bonus extra cast; repeat the cycle.
Attack the dummy continuously between ability casts so basic-attack damage and on-hit effects (including the empowered Savagery stab, when armed) are never left idle.

Continue cycling Q > basic attacks > E/W (on cooldown) > Ferocity dump for the remainder of the 15s window, using R again only if its (80-100s) cooldown somehow completes, which it will not within a single 15s fight after the opener.
questions: Which ability should Rengar prioritize consuming Ferocity into for maximum single-target DPS: Q (crit-capable stab + attack speed) versus E/W's larger flat empowered damage numbers?

Is it correct to open with R despite its very long cooldown and the fact that most of its value (stealth, mark, movement speed) is defensive/positional rather than damage, or should the damage-fight rotation exclude R entirely and treat it as never available?

Does the sim's basic-attack cadence actually let Rengar land the leap/empowered Unseen Predator attack given there is no ally, minion, or terrain to path around, or does the lack of brush make Unseen Predator's leap moot outside of R's camouflage window?

Should Savagery's 'critically strike' clause be treated as dealing bonus crit damage only when the simulated build includes crit chance/damage stats, i.e. is 0% crit (no crit items) the correct baseline assumption for ranking non-crit item builds?
